partials/two: Many functions take more than one input. Here f of u and v is u squared plus two v squared: a bowl, seen from above as rings of equal height.
partials/du: Hold v fixed and move only u. Along that line f is an ordinary curve, and its slope is the partial derivative in u, written partial f, partial u. The curly d, read “partial”, means only u moves, with v held still.
partials/terms: Take f term by term. u squared gives two u. Two v squared does not change while v is held, so it is a constant, and gives zero. So partial f, partial u is two u: two, at the point one, one.
partials/dv: Hold u fixed instead. Now u squared is the constant, and gives zero, while two v squared gives four v. So partial f, partial v is four v: four here.
partials/grad: Stack the partials into a vector, and you have the gradient of f. It is written nabla f, read “nabla f” after the upside-down triangle, called nabla. Here the gradient of f is two, four.
uphill/up: The gradient points the way f climbs fastest: straight up the bowl, across the rings.
uphill/down: To make f smaller, step the other way, against the gradient: along minus nabla f.
uphill/small: A small step, a tenth of the gradient, lands on a lower ring: f drops from three to one point three six.
shape/loss: A function can take a whole grid of numbers as its input. Here W has three rows and four columns, twelve numbers in all, and f turns them into a single number.
shape/g: So the gradient nabla f has twelve partials, one per entry of W, laid out exactly like W: three by four. Since it holds the slopes of f in the entries of W, it is also written partial f, partial W.
shape/entry: Each entry says how f moves when that one number in W is nudged: the gradient at row one, column two belongs to W at row one, column two.
mixed/mix: Some terms mix the inputs. Take f of u and v is u squared plus three u v, at the point u equals one, v equals two.
mixed/held: For the partial in u, hold v at two. Then three u v is three times two times u: six u, a line in u with slope six. And six is three times v.
mixed/pu: So a held v acts as a number multiplying u, and three u v gives three v. With u squared giving two u, partial f, partial u is two u plus three v: two plus six, eight.
mixed/pv: For the partial in v, hold u at one. u squared is a constant, giving zero. Three u v is three v, giving three, which is three u. So partial f, partial v is three u: three.
mixed/both: Stack them: at one, two, the gradient is eight, three.
mixed/p1: Try one. f of u and v is two u squared, plus u v, plus four v. What is nabla f at one, two?
mixed/a1u: In u, with v held: two u squared gives four u, u v gives v, and four v gives zero. Four plus two is six.
mixed/a1v: In v, with u held: two u squared gives zero, u v gives u, and four v gives four. One plus four is five. So nabla f is six, five.
mixed/p2: One more. f of u and v is u squared v, plus two v squared, plus three u. What is partial f, partial u at two, one?
mixed/a2: Hold v. u squared v is v times u squared, so it gives v times two u: two u v. Two v squared gives zero, and three u gives three. Two times two times one, plus three: seven.
